stem.text: Two waves, P and Q, meet at a point X and superpose.
Initially, the two waves meet at X in phase (zero phase difference) so that the resultant wave has an amplitude of $14.0\,\text{cm}$ at that point.
The phase difference between the two waves is then changed so that they meet at X with a phase difference of $180^{\circ}$. The resultant wave now has an amplitude of $4.0\,\text{cm}$ at X.
What is the amplitude of one of the waves at point X?
